Issued at 235 PM EDT Thu Aug 6 2026

Through Tonight...Scattered showers and storms continue to 
develop and move westward across the Florida peninsula this 
afternoon, with coverage anticipated to continue increasing as 
activity moves farther inland, especially near and west of the I-4
corridor. Limited cloud coverage earlier in the day supported 
adequate daytime heating prior to the start of convective 
development, with temperatures remaining on track to reach the 
upper 80s to low 90s areawide. Analyzed MLCAPE exceeds 2000 J/kg 
areawide and lifted index values range between -8 to -6. DCAPE 
remains generally between 600-900 J/kg and 500 mb temperatures 
range between -9C to -8C across east central Florida. Based on 
this environment, anticipate storms to produce frequent lightning 
strikes, wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph, heavy downpours that could 
lead to brief, localized flooding in some spots, and even small 
hail. Strong easterly flow aloft will keep activity moving towards
the west and northwest at 10 to 15 mph through this afternoon, 
with activity gradually diminishing late this afternoon into this 
evening across the peninsula. While mostly dry conditions are 
forecast across the peninsula later today, there is a chance for 
continued isolated to scattered shower and storm development 
across the local Atlantic waters. Some activity may be able to 
move onshore given the persistent easterly flow at the surface and
aloft, especially from the Cape southward. Muggy conditions 
persist into the overnight hours with lows remaining in the mid 
70s areawide. 

Friday-Saturday...An inverted trough situated near the Bahamas is
forecast to lift northward across the Florida peninsula late this
week into the early weekend. Guidance has trended slightly slower
with the trough's arrival and departure across the state, though 
the overall message remains the same: moisture will increase 
areawide. PWAT's of 2.1-2.3" are forecast locally, which will in 
turn translate to higher than normal rain chances (60-80% Friday, 
50-70% Saturday). The higher rain chances extend across the whole 
area on Friday and are favored towards the interior and I-4 
corridor on Saturday, due to the inverted trough lifting north and
away from the area. Storms cannot be ruled out with activity on 
either day thanks to modest MLCAPE of 1500 J/kg and greater, cool 
temperatures aloft ranging from -7C to -6C at 500 mb, and 
downdraft CAPE of 600-900 J/kg. Overall, storm hazards will 
include frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph, 
and with the greater moisture present, heavy downpours. While 
steering flow looks to be sufficient on Friday, some weakening in 
the lower levels on Saturday could lead to a slightly greater risk
of localized flooding across east central Florida. Overall, 
rainfall totals of 2-4" will be possible Friday and Saturday, with
localized higher amounts not able to be ruled out in some 
locations that see multiple rounds of showers or slow-moving 
activity. Activity is anticipated to diminish into the evening and
overnight hours, though persistent onshore flow will support 
continued development across the local Atlantic waters Friday 
night. Saturday night, drier conditions are anticipated areawide.

The greater moisture and in turn greater cloud coverage will work
to help limit daytime heating across east central Florida, 
keeping afternoon temperatures relatively close to normal in the 
upper 80s to low 90s. The moist air mass will keep relative 
humidities high, which will still keep peak heat indices of 
100-107F possible across the area. Overnight lows generally remain
in the mid 70s.

At the beaches, increasing choppy surf from the passing inverted 
trough is anticipated. This means there will likely be an 
increasing risk for rip currents at all local beaches, so caution 
is advised. If necessary, a high risk of rip currents may be 
warranted.

Sunday-Wednesday...Mid-level ridging drifts back towards the 
Florida peninsula early next week, strengthening as it remains 
overhead. At the surface, the Atlantic high will shift southward, 
with the ridge axis once again extending towards the Florida 
peninsula. Lingering moisture in the wake of the inverted trough 
will lead to 40-60% rain and storm chances on Sunday, with values 
returning closer to normal into the start of the work week. Drier 
air aloft looks to move overhead, which will help limit some 
convective development Monday onward. Any activity that does 
develop will be diurnally driven, with the sea breeze the primary 
forcing mechanism for development each afternoon. While exact 
storm threats can't be pinned down at this point, would anticipate
the typical summertime storm hazards all being possible; 
lightning strikes, gusty winds, and heavy downpours. Showers and 
storms will diminish across the peninsula during the late evening 
and overnight hours, with mostly dry conditions across east 
central Florida each night.
